defects: B-WHOLE, seed 1: The conspicuously white, horizontally marked bark and clustered pale stems read as birch rather than the smooth gray trunk shown in the European-beech photographic reference. This defeats mature-beech recognizability; the upright crown itself is not the blocker.

B-BARE, seed 1: The exposed white bark with strong dark horizontal markings gives the tree dominant birch character, unlike the uniformly gray beech bark in the direct bare reference. The very dense hairlike twig network also reads as an obvious construction artifact, although overall finish is not below the spruce quality floor.

observations: B-WHOLE: The dense, rounded deciduous canopy and limited droop are plausible natural variation and otherwise meet or exceed the catalogue anchor's finish level.
B-BARE: The upright crown form alone would not disqualify the tree; reducing visually noisy micro-twigs would be an optional refinement if the species-defining bark is corrected.
